evidence: app/src/pages/ability.ts:1-22 — the whole feature is one self-contained page file
app/src/main.ts:8,31 — feature removal needs an import and a route-table entry here
app/server.mjs:20 — the same route must also be deleted from a duplicated ROUTES regex list or the server 404s it
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:44,118-131 — the Pokémon page's Abilities section and its /abilities links live outside the feature directory
app/src/api.ts:74-89 — the Ability interface and app/src/components.ts:10,32 the CardData.hidden flag exist only for this feature and would become dead code
app/index.html:14-18 — nav is static HTML, so dropping a nav link is a one-line edit
removability.rationale: Pages are individually self-contained and nothing is entangled, but deleting one feature means coordinated edits in four to five files plus dead-code cleanup, which is exactly 'a handful of scattered edits', not delete-and-done.

evidence: app/src/components.ts:21-35 — every card list renders through the single pokemonCard function, so the sprite display fix has one render site
app/src/components.ts:5-10,28 — CardData.id is ambiguous and the sprite is derived from it, so the real fix is a contract change, not a renderer change
app/src/pages/home.ts:87 — home fills CardData.id from the species list
app/src/components.ts:57-58 — cardsFromPokemon fills it from a Pokémon ref URL (deoxys-normal → 386)
app/src/pages/team.ts:20-23 — the team page fills it a third way
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:19-21 — default-variety resolution duplicated verbatim in app/src/pages/team.ts:21-23
app/src/format.ts:9-37 — text rules (humanize, english name, dex number, em dash) are centralized, so most fixes are one-liners
changeability.rationale: Formatting bugs land in one obvious module and all cards render through one function, but the species-vs-default-Pokémon distinction the spec calls out is not modeled anywhere, and the default-variety lookup is copy-pasted, so the concrete bug in the scenario needs coordinated edits across the CardData contract, three producers and a duplicated helper.

evidence: app/src/main.ts:11-15 — pages receive a narrow PageContext (main, url, isCurrent stale-render guard) rather than app internals
app/src/pages/move.ts:6 — pages depend on main only via `import type`, so no runtime cycle between the router and pages
app/src/api.ts:3-11,119-137 — the API base URL and the response cache are known only inside this module
app/src/team.ts:1-3 — team state imports only dom.ts and owns its localStorage key explicitly
app/server.mjs:14-18,20 — the server serves the shell and injects the API origin but contains no app logic; the only leak is the duplicated route regexes
coupling.rationale: Loosely coupled with clear seams: a data layer, a formatting layer, small components, a router that hands pages a narrow context, and a server that stays out of the way. The one real tangle is the client/server route duplication.

evidence: app/src/components.ts:51-60 — cardsFromPokemon's ref/extra callbacks absorb the type/move/ability variation (and the hidden-ability note) without flag params — a well-designed seam
app/src/components.ts:42-46,39 — section() and countLine() are right-sized reusable primitives
app/src/components.ts:5-10 — CardData.id conflates species id and Pokémon id, the one distinction the spec itself hinges on
app/src/components.ts:13 — typeBadge's asLink boolean is mild flag creep
app/src/pages/team.ts:88-96 — the team page bypasses cardList and re-creates the card-grid markup instead of extending the component
app/src/pages/home.ts:46-58 — 'types of each Pokémon' is re-derived by reverse-walking allTypes; a second consumer would derive it again
abstraction_design.rationale: The core abstractions stretch well — one card pipeline covers four different sources, and one section/heading helper covers every page — but the model that matters most (species vs default Pokémon) is implicit, and there is enough local duplication (team's hand-rolled grid, home's type derivation) that similar-but-different changes start costing copy-paste.

findings.issue: Route knowledge is duplicated: the client route table (app/src/main.ts:24-32) is restated as parallel regexes in the server's ROUTES list; forgetting one makes the server return 404 for a page the client can render (and vice versa).
findings.suggestion: Move the route patterns into one shared module (e.g. src/routes.ts) imported by main.ts, and have server.mjs read the same list — or generate the server list at build time from it.

findings.issue: The 'find the default variety and fetch its Pokémon' resolution is copy-pasted verbatim from app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:19-21, so any fix to it (including the Deoxys-style sprite bug) must land twice.
findings.suggestion: Extract a `defaultPokemon(species): Promise<Pokemon>` helper into app/src/api.ts next to the Species/Pokemon interfaces and use it from both pages.

findings.issue: CardData.id conflates species id and Pokémon id; the sprite is derived from it (components.ts:28), which is precisely why species whose default Pokémon differs (Deoxys) can render the wrong sprite, and the three producers fill it three different ways (home.ts:87, components.ts:57-58, team.ts:20-23).
findings.suggestion: Make CardData carry the species name/id plus an explicit sprite URL (or a front_default fetched once), so the species/Pokémon distinction is modeled at the seam instead of papered over in each producer.

findings.issue: The team page hand-rolls `<ul class="card-grid">` and per-item card markup instead of extending cardList/pokemonCard, duplicating the card-grid structure and the card-item wrapper.
findings.suggestion: Extend cardList with an optional per-item footer/extra node (a callback, not a boolean) so the remove button is attached through the same component every other list uses.

findings.issue: The 'types of each default Pokémon' dataset is derived ad hoc inside the home page by reverse-walking all 18 type payloads; any other consumer of per-Pokémon types would re-derive it.
findings.suggestion: Promote a `typesByPokemonId()` helper into app/src/api.ts (cached) next to allTypes().

findings.issue: typeBadge takes an asLink boolean flag, the beginning of flag-parameter creep.
findings.suggestion: Two tiny functions (typeBadgeLink / typeBadgeSpan) or an explicit `variant` union reads more clearly at call sites.

findings.issue: The app itself ships zero tests (0 test files/cases per static analysis); every refactor — including all five scenarios here — is only verified by the repo-root acceptance suite, which the app can't extend for regressions.
findings.suggestion: Add a lightweight vitest suite covering the pure seams that carry the risk: format.ts helpers, cardsFromPokemon mapping, team.ts state, and the api.ts URL builder.

summary: A genuinely pleasant small vanilla-TS app to edit: clear layers (api/format/dom/components/pages), a narrow PageContext with a stale-render guard, and one card pipeline that four different data sources feed into. The consistent friction is that anything touching routes or the species-vs-default-Pokémon distinction requires coordinated edits in several files, including a verbatim client/server route duplication and a copy-pasted default-variety lookup. Fixing the CardData contract and sharing the route table would move this from 'fine' to 'easy'.

No nav link to remove, since nav is static in index.html.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules

New rules are one module, plus the injection mechanism if the transport itself changes.
